title: Training Q&A — Late-Fee History Share on Utility Pass-Through Service Late Fees
content:
**Rule.** For a late fee on a Utility Pass-Through Service statement, an account with no utility late fee posted in the last twelve months pays 50 percent of the fee basis, and an account with three or more utility late fees posted in the last twelve months pays 150 percent of it (a multiplier of 1.5). An account with one or two takes no history share under this rule.

## Questions answered

**Q. Which late fees are counted?** Utility late fees already posted on the Utility Pass-Through Service account, by posting date, where fewer than 12 whole months separate the posting date from the handling date. Late fees on other accounts or ledgers are not counted here.

**Q. What is the fee basis?** The amount the statement's late fee is figured from; the share multiplies it, and the fee is rounded half up to the cent once, on the final figure.

**Q. The shares at a glance?**

| Utility late fees posted in the last 12 months | Share of the fee basis |
|---|---|
| 0 | 50 percent |
| 1 or 2 | no share under this rule |
| 3 or more | 150 percent |

**Q. Worked through (hypothetical fee basis 12.00).** No late fee in the last 12 months: 12.00 times 50 percent is 6.00. Three late fees in that span: 12.00 times 1.5 is 18.00.

**Q. A late fee posted exactly twelve whole months before the handling date?** It is not in the last twelve months and is not counted.
